memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'I will look on you with favor and make you fruitful and increase your
numbers, and I will keep my covenant with you'" - Lev 26:9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice the wonderful phrase: I will look on you with favor. The Hebrew
carries the sense of God turning His face towards His people, giving them
His full attention and care. In a chapter full of blessings, this is the
heart of them all — not the gifts, but the Giver turning towards you.

The greatest blessing was never the crops or the safety. It was God
Himself drawing near and keeping His covenant.

Dear reader, we sometimes want God's gifts more than we want God. We pray
for the healing, the provision, the open door — and forget that the
deepest treasure is God turning His face towards us.

Do you remember the ancient blessing God gave Israel? The Lord make His
face shine on you and be gracious to you; the Lord turn His face towards
you and give you peace (Num 6:25-26). It is the same beautiful image.

And here is the gospel wonder: in Christ, God has turned His face towards
us permanently. Paul writes that God has blessed us in the Beloved and
made us accepted (Eph 1:6). The favour of God rests on us not because we
have earned it but because we are in His Son.

At the cross, Jesus experienced God turning away — my God, why have you
forsaken me — so that God could turn His face towards us forever.

The favour of God is not a distant hope. In Christ, it is yours.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I long for God's gifts more than for God Himself?
2. Do I live as though God's face is turned towards me in Christ?
3. How does knowing God favours me in Christ change my day?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that in Christ You have turned Your face towards me
forever. Help me treasure Your presence above every gift, and rest in
Your favour. Amen.
